plain.li: [opt0,safe] Mushrooms came up after the rain. Two baskets of the good kind are drying in the storeroom.
[opt0,risk] Half the mushrooms we brought in were the bitter kind. The other half were good. I've learned which is which now, the hard way.
[opt1] Wild mushrooms for supper. I found them, so I got the first plate.
[opt2] Found a ring of mushrooms out past the fields. We left them be. Probably wise.
Mushrooms everywhere after the rain. The whole place smells of them.

warm.li: [opt1] The others ate the mushrooms I found. Small thing, but I liked watching them eat.

blunt.li: [opt2] Food growing out of the ground and we left it there.

cheerful.li: [opt1] Mushroom supper! I'd go out in the rain every day for that.

gloomy.li: [opt2] The mushrooms will rot where they stand.

cold.li: [opt0] Two baskets of edible fungus, sorted and checked. A useful morning.

plain.li: [opt0] Stayed up all night with everyone. The sun went down behind the hill and came straight back up.
[opt1] Blankets over the windows. It's still light behind them. I counted the threads until I slept.
[opt2] We get to sleep late tomorrow. Just as well. The sun hasn't gone down, and neither have I.
Midnight, and I can read this page without a candle.

warm.li: [opt0] Sat up with everyone through the bright night. The best night we've had here.

blunt.li: [opt1] Can't sleep. Sun won't go down.

cheerful.li: [opt0] We danced at midnight in broad daylight. I'm still giddy.

gloomy.li: Three nights without dark. I'm so tired I could weep.

cold.li: [opt1] Usual hours kept. The work will not suffer for a bright sky.

plain.li: [opt0] First snow, and the council called a snow day. I got hit in the ear by a snowball and don't know who threw it.
[opt1] First snow of the year. Shoveled paths until my arms ached.
I was the first one out in the snow this morning. My footprints were the only ones for an hour.
[opt0] Built a snow wall by the storeroom. It's leaning already.

warm.li: [opt0] Everyone out in the snow together, red-faced and laughing. I'll keep this one.

cheerful.li: [opt0] Snow day! I haven't had one of those since I was small.

gloomy.li: The first snow. That means the long cold is coming.

cold.li: [opt0] The council stopped work for snow. A day of production lost to throwing it at each other.

plain.li: [opt0] We kept the fire going all through the longest night. Saw the sun come back with ash in my hair.
[opt1] Good supper for the longest night, then bed. I like a sensible holiday.
[opt2] Longest night of the year. The others didn't want to make anything of it. I sat up a while anyway.
[lowtech,opt0] Fed the fire till dawn the way my people do. The sun came back. It always does, but you have to help.

warm.li: [opt0] Sat up all night with all of them round the fire. I'd do it every winter.

blunt.li: [opt0] Fed the fire all night. Worth the wood, I suppose.

cheerful.li: [opt0] We cheered when the sky went gray! It felt like we'd done it ourselves.

gloomy.li: The longest night. It felt longer than that.

cold.li: [opt2] The longest night passed like any other. It is only a night.

plain.li: [opt0] A scribe wrote my letter home today. I said more than I meant to, and {X_nameDef} wrote all of it down.
[opt1] Told the colony's story to a scribe, from the first day on. It sounded bigger told out loud.
[opt2] The scribe taught us our letters. I can write my name now. I wrote it four times on the table.
[opt3] A scribe came and went. I'd have liked to send a letter.

warm.li: [opt0] My letter is on its way home. Someone there will cry over it, I hope in a good way.

blunt.li: [opt0] Paid a stranger to write my business down. Strange times.

cheerful.li: [opt2] I can write now. Badly, but I can!

gloomy.li: [opt0] Wrote home. I don't know who's left there to read it.

cold.li: [opt1] The colony's history is written down at last. Useful, the next time there's a dispute about who did what.

plain.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} from the glitterworld asked me where the water comes from. Then again at supper. Then again at breakfast.
[opt1,safe] Watched {X_nameDef} muck out the barn in a silk shirt. Paid us extra for the privilege.
[opt1,risk] The tourist lasted half a day of real work and asked for a refund. Got half. Still more than I make.
[opt2] A tourist came to look at how we live, took pictures of the gate and left. We're not a zoo.

warm.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} was hopeless at everything and very sweet about it. I'll miss the questions.

blunt.li: [opt0] Rich fool paid good silver to sleep on our floor. Fine by me.

cheerful.li: [opt1] I taught a glitterworlder to use a shovel. Wrong end first, but we got there.

gloomy.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} will go home and tell everyone how hard we have it, and then forget us.

cold.li: [opt0] A tourist paid for an experience. We sold one. A clean transaction.

plain.li: [opt0] A traveling healer saw to my {TALE} today. Whatever was in that tea, it's working.
[opt1] {X_nameDef} fixed my {TALE} with our doctor watching every move. I felt like a lesson.
[opt2] A healer offered to see to my {TALE} and I said I'd manage. I'm managing. Mostly.
[opt0] Stranger's hands, stranger's medicine, and the {TALE} is better already. I won't ask what was in it.

warm.li: [opt0] The council paid for a healer for me. I didn't think anyone noticed I was hurting.

blunt.li: [opt2] Don't need a stranger poking at me. It'll pass.

cheerful.li: [opt0] Good as new, nearly. Better than yesterday!

gloomy.li: [opt2] The {TALE} again. Turned the healer away. Regretting it.

cold.li: [opt1] The healer's methods were crude but effective. Our doctor took notes.

plain.li: [opt0] A musician played just for me, out by the woodpile after dark. I fell asleep sitting up. First real sleep in days.
[opt1] Music after supper for everyone. I sat near the front. It helped more than I expected.
[opt2] A musician offered to play for me. I said no. I don't want to be the one who needs it.
[opt0] {X_nameDef} didn't ask me anything, just played. That was exactly right.

warm.li: [opt0] Someone I'd never met sat with me half the night and played. People can be very kind.

blunt.li: [opt0] Didn't want a song. Got one anyway. Slept like the dead.

cheerful.li: [opt1] Music and dancing. I'd forgotten I could dance!

gloomy.li: [opt0] The music helped tonight. Tomorrow it'll be the same as before.

cold.li: [opt0] A stranger played for me because I looked tired. I did not know it showed.

plain.li: [opt0,safe] A peacemaker sat me down across from someone I can't stand. We talked until midnight. I can stand them now, nearly.
[opt0,risk] A peacemaker tried to patch things up between me and someone here. It didn't take. At least we both tried.
[opt1] The council has us rebuilding the woodpile together. We argued about every log.
[opt2] A peacemaker offered to sort out my quarrel, and went on without doing it. Fine. It's mine to sort.

warm.li: [opt0,safe] We shook hands at the end. I think we both meant it.

blunt.li: [opt1] Made to work beside someone I don't like. We stacked wood. Badly.

cheerful.li: [opt0,safe] Half a night at that table with the peacemaker, and we came out of it laughing!

gloomy.li: [opt0,risk] Some things don't mend. I knew that before the peacemaker came.

cold.li: [opt0] A stranger arbitrated my grievances. It was efficient, I'll give {X_objective} that.

plain.li: [opt0] A peddler had food from home, and the council bought it for me. I had to sit down after the first bite.
[opt1] I cooked supper from home for everyone tonight. Half of them made faces. All of them had seconds.
[opt2] Saw food from home on a peddler's blanket today. Walked past it. Thought about it all afternoon.
[opt0] I'm rationing it. One a day. It has to last.

warm.li: [opt1] Fed everyone the food I grew up on and told them where it came from. It felt like having them over.

blunt.li: [opt2] No taste of home for me. Fine. It wasn't that good anyway.

cheerful.li: [opt0] It tastes exactly the way I remember. I could cry.

gloomy.li: [opt0] It tastes like home. That's the trouble with it.

cold.li: [opt0] Purchased a nostalgic foodstuff. Effective on morale. Mine, at least.

plain.li: [opt0,safe] {X_nameDef} came all this way to say sorry. We talked for hours. I don't hate {X_objective} anymore, and I don't know what to do with the space.
[opt0,risk] Let {X_nameDef} in to apologize. Should have kept the door shut. It's all fresh again.
[opt1] {X_nameDef} stayed for supper. It was strange, laughing with {X_objective}. Strange and good.
[opt2] {X_nameDef} came to the gate. I didn't go out. Some things stay where you left them.

warm.li: [opt0,safe] I forgave {X_nameDef}. I think I'd been waiting years for the chance.

cheerful.li: [opt1] An old enemy at our table, and the soup was good. Life is odd!

gloomy.li: [opt0,risk] Sorry doesn't give back the years.

cold.li: [opt0,safe] {X_nameDef} paid what was owed, with interest. The account is closed.

plain.li: [opt0] Had it out with {X_nameDef} from the camp. The council backed me. The camp isn't speaking to me now.
[opt1] The camp gets to keep it, to keep the peace. My peace wasn't asked about.
[opt2,safe] One of ours talked me and {X_nameDef} round to splitting it. We shook on it in front of the whole camp.
[opt2,risk] They tried to settle it between me and {X_nameDef}. Went round in circles until dark.

warm.li: [opt1] Let the camp have it. They've less than we do, I suppose.

blunt.li: [opt0] It was mine. The council agreed. Good.

cheerful.li: [opt2,safe] Half each and a handshake. {X_nameDef} isn't so bad, really.

gloomy.li: [opt1] Strangers camp on our land and take what's ours, and we give them more.

cold.li: [opt0] Precedent established. The camp will think twice.
